proof:
The finite union of the retained placed fibers is compact and lies in $Q$, so its convex hull is compact and contained in $Q$. Its base projection is $\operatorname{conv}P\subset F$. At a lattice base $p$ of this projection, the hull has a nonempty fiber. If $P$ keeps all nonempty fibers, containment in $Q$ places $p$ in $P$. If $P$ keeps positive fibers, write $p=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i$ with $p_i\in P$, $\lambda_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Fix one index $j$ with $\lambda_j>0$ and one point of $Q_{p_i}$ for every $i\ne j$. Their weighted sum plus $\lambda_j Q_{p_j}$ lies in $(Q_P)_p$ and has positive $s$-volume. Hence $Q_p$ has positive volume, so again $p\in P$. At every $p\in P$ the whole original fiber was included among the generators. Together with containment this proves the equality and rules out extra lattice fibers, including extra nonempty fibers of volume zero.

The base projection affinely spans $A$, and one positive-volume retained fiber supplies all $s$ vertical directions. Thus the affine span of $Q_P$ is $A\times\mathbb R^s$. Write $V=A-p_0$. Its spanning vectors can be chosen among differences of points of $P$, which lie in $L$. The group $V\cap L$ is discrete and contains $t$ independent vectors, so it is a rank-$t$ lattice in $V$. It is saturated since $j\ell\in V\cap L$ for $\ell\in L$ and a nonzero integer $j$ implies $\ell\in V$. Translating by $p_0$ gives $(a+L)\cap A=p_0+(V\cap L)$. A basis of this full induced lattice, with the identity on the continuous coordinate, sends the retained hull to a convex body with exactly the corresponding standard integer fibers. It leaves their Euclidean $s$-volumes unchanged.

For the retained source, a containing ambient closed halfspace restricts to a containing relative closed halfspace or the whole relative space, and every relative closed halfspace extends to an ambient one by extending its defining affine functional. The coordinate identification is affine and so preserves these halfspace tests and their masses. The raw comparison is the restriction argument of accepted fact ba0f3db1bf4f62c6. Each original containing cap has at least the mass of its retained trace, which in turn has at least the retained raw depth at the point. This also applies when $Q$ is a fixed coarse slice. Empty original fibers may be omitted and zero-volume fibers contribute zero mass to every cap. The retained hull realizes exactly the indicated family and supplies its full intrinsic ambient space.

For $t>0$ apply the assumed sharp bound to this full-dimensional convex body of positive sampled mass $T_P$. If $t=0$, the retained hull is a single full-dimensional continuous body of volume $T_P$. In accepted fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d take $d=s$ and $m=a=T_P$. Its full-mass metronoid is the centroid, giving at least $\Gamma_s T_P$ in every containing continuous halfspace. The whole-space restriction also has this much mass. The raw comparison then gives the stated original guarantee.

source_sections.locator: §3, all nonempty fibers on a rank-deficient level

statement:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^s$ be compact and convex, with $s\ge1$, and let $a+L$ be a full-rank lattice coset in $\mathbb R^r$. Let $F\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be an affine subspace. Take $P$ to consist of either all the lattice bases in $F$ with nonempty $Q$-fibers or all the lattice bases in $F$ with positive $s$-volume $Q$-fibers. Assume the sum $T_P$ of the retained fiber volumes is positive. Put $A=\operatorname{aff}P$, $t=\dim A$, and
$$
Q_P=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times Q_p).
$$
For every $p\in(a+L)\cap A$ the fiber $(Q_P)_p$ equals $Q_p$ if $p\in P$ and is empty otherwise. The hull is a full-dimensional compact convex body in $A\times\mathbb R^s$. For any $p_0\in P$, the lattice there is $p_0+(L\cap(A-p_0))$, whose difference lattice is saturated in $L$ and has rank $t$. A lattice basis gives an affine identification with $\mathbb R^t\times\mathbb R^s$ and sample lattice $\mathbb Z^t\times\mathbb R^s$, preserving every fiber volume and the raw halfspace depth within the retained source. For every retained candidate, its raw depth in the original source is at least its retained raw depth. The same comparison holds if $Q$ is a fixed coarse slice of a larger original source.

For $t>0$, assume the sharp mixed-integer bound in dimensions $(t,s)$, namely that every full-dimensional compact convex body of positive sampled mass in those dimensions has a sampled point of normalized depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s$, where $\Gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$. Then some retained point has raw depth at least $2^{-t}\Gamma_s T_P$ in the original source. At $t=0$ the same conclusion holds unconditionally.
title: Exact lattice fibers in the hull of a retained affine slice
